source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Human Reproduction
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Interstitial cells of Leydig in the human testis secrete
questions.explanation: Leydig cells in the interstitial tissue produce testosterone under LH stimulation.

questions.stem: The funnel-shaped opening of the oviduct that receives the ovulated oocyte is the
questions.explanation: The infundibulum, with fimbriae, collects the oocyte from the ovarian surface.

questions.stem: Conversion of haploid spermatids into spermatozoa is termed
questions.explanation: Spermiogenesis is the morphological transformation of spermatids; spermiation is later release into the lumen.

questions.stem: The first polar body in humans is extruded when the
options: sperm is produced in the epididymis
secondary oocyte is still in the fetal ovary
questions.explanation: Meiosis I of the primary oocyte yields a secondary oocyte and the first polar body, usually around ovulation.

questions.stem: In a typical 28-day menstrual cycle, ovulation is triggered by a mid-cycle surge of
questions.explanation: A sharp LH peak from the anterior pituitary causes rupture of the mature Graafian follicle.

questions.stem: The enzyme-filled cap of the spermatozoon that helps it penetrate egg coats is the
questions.explanation: The acrosome is a Golgi-derived cap with hyaluronidase and acrosin used in the acrosome reaction.

questions.stem: The outer cellular layer of the blastocyst that later forms chorionic tissue is the
questions.explanation: Trophoblast cells enclose the blastocoel and contribute extra-embryonic membranes and placenta.

questions.stem: After the first trimester, progesterone needed to keep the uterus quiescent is produced mainly by the
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum is the early source; later the placenta takes over progesterone secretion.

questions.stem: The three primary germ layers of the embryo are established during
questions.explanation: Gastrulation rearranges the bilaminar disc into ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.

questions.stem: The posterior-pituitary hormone that causes ejection of milk from mammary alveoli is
questions.explanation: Oxytocin contracts myoepithelial cells around alveoli (milk ejection); prolactin drives milk synthesis.

questions.stem: Seminal plasma in humans is contributed mainly by the
options: seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands
questions.explanation: Accessory glands add fructose, prostaglandins, enzymes and mucus that make up most of the semen volume.

questions.stem: If fertilisation does not occur, the corpus luteum
options: remains active for the full nine months
questions.explanation: Without hCG support the corpus luteum regresses, progesterone falls and menstruation follows.

questions.stem: A human secondary oocyte completes meiosis II
options: only after a spermatozoon has entered
inside the fetal ovary before birth
automatically at the moment of ovulation
questions.explanation: Ovulation releases a secondary oocyte arrested at metaphase II; sperm entry triggers completion of meiosis II.

questions.stem: Sertoli cells lining seminiferous tubules primarily
options: nourish developing germ cells and form the blood–testis barrier
secrete testosterone into the interstitial fluid
construct the zona pellucida of the ovum
questions.explanation: Sertoli (nurse) cells support spermatogenesis and secrete inhibin; Leydig cells make testosterone.

questions.stem: The uterine layer that is shed during menstruation is the
questions.explanation: Falling progesterone causes breakdown of the functional endometrium; myometrium is muscle, perimetrium is serosa.

questions.stem: One primary spermatocyte that completes meiosis typically yields
questions.explanation: Meiosis of a primary spermatocyte produces four haploid spermatids that differentiate into spermatozoa.

questions.stem: At birth, oocytes in the human ovary are arrested at
questions.explanation: Primary oocytes remain in dictyotene (diplotene of prophase I) until the ovulatory cycle resumes meiosis I.

questions.stem: Menstrual bleeding begins mainly because of withdrawal of
questions.explanation: Regression of the corpus luteum drops progesterone (and oestrogen), so the endometrium is shed.

questions.stem: Capacitation, which makes spermatozoa competent to fertilise, occurs in the
questions.explanation: Secretions of the female tract remove inhibitory coating from sperm and enable the acrosome reaction.

questions.stem: The inner cell mass of the blastocyst gives rise to the
questions.explanation: The embryoblast (inner cell mass) forms the embryo; trophoblast forms extra-embryonic tissue.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect statement about the human placenta.
options: It is formed only by maternal endometrial tissue
It permits exchange of nutrients and gases
It secretes hCG in early pregnancy
It functions as a temporary endocrine gland
questions.explanation: The placenta is foeto-maternal: chorionic villi (fetal) plus decidua (maternal).

questions.stem: The extra-embryonic membrane that contributes most directly to the human placenta is the
questions.explanation: Chorionic villi invade the endometrium and, with decidua, form the discoid placenta.

questions.stem: Colostrum, the first milk after delivery, is especially rich in
questions.explanation: Colostrum supplies maternal antibodies, chiefly IgA, that protect the newborn gut.

questions.stem: Fructose that spermatozoa use as an energy source is added mainly by the
questions.explanation: Seminal vesicles secrete a fructose-rich alkaline fluid that is the largest fraction of semen.

questions.stem: Which event does not belong to the proliferative (follicular) phase of the menstrual cycle?
options: formation of a fully developed corpus luteum
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum forms after ovulation and characterises the luteal (secretory) phase.

questions.stem: Polar bodies produced during oogenesis are
options: diploid nurse cells of the follicle
four functional ova from each primary oocyte
questions.explanation: Unequal cytokinesis yields one ovum and polar bodies that discard extra haploid sets and normally die.
